title: Chapter 1
subtitle: You learned about prenatal care and the importance EPI Vaccines.

questions.question: What is a EPI?

answers.text: Expanded Program on Immunization
Emergency Program for Infants
Early Protection for Illness
Essential Program for Infants

questions.explanation: EPI or Expanded Program on Immunization is a program that helps protect children from vaccine-preventable diseases.

questions.question: What is a vaccine?

answers.text: A medicine that helps the body build protection against diseases
A medicine that treats a disease after a person gets sick
A medicine that prevents a person from getting any illness
A medicine that replaces the body's natural immune system

questions.explanation: A vaccine helps the body build protection against specific diseases.

questions.question: What can happen if a vaccine is delayed?

answers.text: The baby may stay unprotected for longer
The vaccine will no longer work
The baby will become immune to the disease naturally
The next vaccine will no longer be needed

questions.explanation: Delaying a vaccine can leave a baby unprotected for longer.

questions.question: What should parents do if they are unsure about vaccines?

answers.text: Ask doctors, nurses,or health workers
Search random online posts
Ignore the information completely
Skip vaccinations

questions.explanation: If parents are unsure about vaccines they should ask a healthcare provider for accurate information.

questions.question: What do vaccines do?

answers.text: They lower the risk of getting serious diseases
They make a person completely immune to all diseases
They guarantee that a person will never get sick
They remove the risk of infection completely

questions.explanation: Vaccines do not give complete protection, but they lower the risk of getting and becoming seriously ill from specific diseases.
